issues.title: [RYAN][GIT] Branch & Worktree Stewardship — protect main, sandbox by Core/Layer/Domain
issues.description:
Companion owner: Ryan. Doctor project manager: Doctor 13. Gatekeeper: Rick S1.

Purpose: make Git the code-isolation layer, not the orchestration source of truth.

Fractal contract:

* Linear Project = Core.
* Companion parent issue = durable responsibility + Activity journal.
* Sub-issues = Doctor-planned executable tasks.
* Orca Project/Worktree = execution projection and sandbox, optionally grouped by Division/Process Control.
* Git main = integration-only, never dirty development.
* Feature branches/worktrees = bounded sandboxes by Core / Layer / Domain.
* End of project = preserve evidence, merge/promote accepted property, archive obsolete branch/worktree; never destroy an unclassified dirty tree.

Branch namespace:
sandbox/<core>/<companion>/<purpose>
feature/<core>/<layer-or-domain>/<purpose>
fix/<core>/<layer-or-domain>/<purpose>
archive/<yyyy-mm>/<source>

Acceptance:

1. Current local+origin branches classified.
2. A clean Ryan governance worktree exists from origin/main without touching the dirty main worktree.
3. main-protection policy is documented and enforcement path identified.
4. Legacy Jules/feature branches are mapped to keep/merge/archive/delete-candidate; no blind deletion.
5. Orca worktrees are created from explicit canonical branches, not unknown origin/\* refs.

issues.title: [BEDROCK] Audit & rebuild Desktop Commander remote access — idempotent, antifragile, durable
issues.description:
## Executive mandate

Audit **Desktop Commander / Remote MCP on Amd-PC from first principles**, identify every source of fragility, and rebuild the access path so it is **idempotent, antifragile, durable, observable, and boring**.

This is a bounded Tech OS / Kernel Core recovery mandate.
Do **not** turn Desktop Commander into a new product or permanent side-project.

## Why this exists

The current DC path has accumulated overlapping wrappers, aliases, supervisors, Scheduled Tasks, stale OAuth sessions, competing launch modes, and partial upgrade attempts. The result has alternated between:

* `Device ready` in foreground manual mode
* broker showing the device offline
* `phase: connecting`
* `phase: retry_wait`
* `Remote exited (1)`
* `Device startup failed: fetch failed`
* `Invalid Refresh Token: Already Used`
* stale/expired device codes
* a PowerShell alias intercepting `desktop-commander`
* multiple generations of wrappers around a tool that should be simple

The objective is not to patch one symptom.
The objective is to **remove accidental complexity and leave one canonical path**.

---

## Current known topology / artifacts to audit

At minimum inspect:

### Installed package / launchers

* `C:\Users\amado\AppData\Roaming\npm\desktop-commander.cmd`
* global npm package `@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander`
* currently observed installed version: `0.2.48`
* attempted upgrade/staging of `0.2.51` was interrupted / not proven complete
* any npm shims / node path used by the command

### PowerShell wrappers / aliases

* `C:\Users\amado\dc.ps1`
* PowerShell profile:
  `C:\Users\amado\Documents\PowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`
* known alias/function:
  `function global:desktop-commander { & 'C:\Users\amado\dc.ps1' @args }`
* any `dc` alias/function

### Scheduled execution / persistence

* Scheduled Task: **ASpace Desktop Commander**
* legacy action observed:
  `wscript.exe //B //NoLogo C:\Users\amado\.desktop-commander\managed\silent.vbs Supervisor`
* later replacement attempt with:
  `direct-runner.ps1`
* task restart policy / multiple-instance semantics / logon trigger

### Legacy management layer

Under:
`C:\Users\amado\.desktop-commander\managed\`

Audit at least:

* `supervisor.mjs`
* `silent.vbs`
* `direct-runner.ps1`
* state files
* launcher logs
* retry/backoff behavior
* child PID management

### Remote identity / logs

* `C:\Users\amado\.desktop-commander\remote.log`
* any Remote Device identity/session store used by the current version
* any backup copies created during prior recovery attempts
* device ID currently expected:
  `c22e1bb6-79bd-4aae-8ee0-c5f06a856654`
* device name: `Amd-PC`

### Network / environment

* Windows user context: `amd-pc\amado`
* `USERPROFILE=C:\Users\amado`
* `APPDATA=C:\Users\amado\AppData\Roaming`
* system/user proxy state
* `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`
* any residual router/proxy process affecting Remote MCP
* TLS / DNS / fetch behavior to `https://mcp.desktopcommander.app`

---

## Required investigation

### 1. Establish ground truth before mutation

Capture:

* installed package version
* exact binary/shim path
* exact command required for Remote mode for that installed version
* active processes and parent/child tree
* Scheduled Task definition
* PowerShell aliases/functions
* auth/session files actually read by Remote mode
* current network/proxy environment
* reproducible foreground behavior
* reproducible background/Scheduled Task behavior

Do not assume the current wrappers are correct.

### 2. Root-cause every observed failure

Explain with evidence:

* why foreground Remote can reach `Device ready`
* why persisted/background mode has failed
* why `Invalid Refresh Token: Already Used` occurred
* why `fetch failed` occurred
* whether concurrency caused refresh-token rotation races
* whether Scheduled Task environment differs materially
* whether custom wrappers cause startup or retry defects
* whether the installed DC version contains a known upstream defect
* whether an upgrade is actually required

### 3. Minimize architecture

Target the smallest reliable topology.

Preferred end-state if technically valid:

```
Windows logon
    ↓
ONE native Scheduled Task
    ↓
ONE canonical DC Remote command
    ↓
Remote MCP
```

Any extra wrapper/supervisor must justify its existence with a capability Windows/DC does not already provide.

### 4. Idempotence

Repeated execution of the canonical repair/start operation must converge to the same healthy state.

Requirements:

* no duplicate processes
* no duplicate Remote devices
* no duplicate OAuth flows
* no stale competing Scheduled Tasks
* no refresh-token races
* safe to run after crash/reboot
* safe to run when already healthy
* no destructive cleanup of unrelated processes

### 5. Antifragility

The system must recover predictably from:

* DC process crash
* reboot/logoff/login
* transient network failure
* Remote MCP outage
* stale token / expired authorization
* package update
* task restart
* orphaned process
* partial prior recovery

Recovery must be bounded and observable.
No infinite opaque retry loops.

### 6. Durable observability

Leave one canonical health signal and one canonical log location.

Health must distinguish at least:

* OFFLINE
* STARTING
* AUTH_REQUIRED
* CONNECTING
* SERVICE_READY
* RETRY_WAIT
* DEGRADED / ERROR

A stale broker record must never be reported as healthy.

### 7. Authentication

Use one canonical persisted identity/session.

Rules:

* never run multiple Remote agents against the same rotating refresh token unless upstream explicitly supports it
* never loop device authorization
* never auto-select credentials or bypass human auth
* when interactive auth is required, surface exactly one bounded action to A0

### 8. Upgrade policy

Do not upgrade merely because a newer version exists.

If an upgrade is required:

* prove why
* stage/test safely first
* preserve rollback
* verify exact version after install
* verify Remote mode end-to-end
* remove obsolete version only after acceptance passes

If current version is repairable and stable, document why staying pinned is preferable.

---

## Forbidden patterns

Do NOT:

* create supervisor-on-supervisor stacks
* create wrapper-on-wrapper aliases
* leave both foreground and background Remote agents running
* create another device identity as a workaround
* silently delete auth state before understanding it
* repeatedly reinstall npm packages as diagnosis
* use destructive `Remove-Item` cleanup without evidence
* treat `process exists` as `Remote healthy`
* report success without a remote call from ChatGPT proving the complete path
* turn DC into a blocking objective for unrelated Tech OS work

---

## Acceptance criteria

The issue can move to **Done** only when all are true:

 1. **Single canonical architecture documented.**
 2. **Single canonical launcher/start command documented.**
 3. **Single canonical Scheduled Task** (if persistence is needed).
 4. No obsolete DC wrapper/process participates in runtime.
 5. No duplicate live Remote agents.
 6. PowerShell aliases no longer shadow or distort the real DC CLI unexpectedly.
 7. Device auth succeeds and persists across process restart.
 8. Reboot/logon persistence is proven or a precise bounded limitation is documented.
 9. Remote device reaches **SERVICE_READY**.
10. A **real remote ping from ChatGPT** succeeds.
11. A **real remote command from ChatGPT** succeeds.
12. Re-running the start/repair action while healthy produces no duplicate or regression.
13. Killing the DC process and letting recovery occur produces one healthy replacement.
14. Logs clearly show lifecycle and error cause.
15. Rollback path is documented and tested.
16. Legacy files are either:
    * removed after proof they are obsolete, or
    * archived with clear non-runtime status.
17. Final evidence is posted to this Linear issue.
18. Any resulting durable architecture change is recorded in the Tech OS canon / AGENTS documentation only after validation.

---

## Deliverables

Produce:

* root-cause report
* before/after architecture diagram
* exact canonical launcher
* exact Scheduled Task definition
* exact health-check procedure
* auth/session lifecycle description
* failure/recovery matrix
* rollback procedure
* evidence of idempotence
* evidence of remote ChatGPT end-to-end success
* list of deleted/archived legacy artifacts
* final recommendation: pinned version + upgrade policy

---

## Execution ownership

This issue may be handed to **Antigravity** for deep audit/reconciliation or to **Hermes** for orchestration.

If Hermes owns it:

* use Orca as ADE
* delegate bounded technical investigation/repair to the appropriate harness
* keep Linear as the human-readable mandate/action ledger
* keep `uc.db / WorkGraph` as sovereign runtime truth where applicable
* record meaningful action deltas here
* do not escalate terminal/PID/plumbing details to A0 unless an irreversible decision or external authentication is required

## Definition of success

Desktop Commander becomes a **boring infrastructure primitive**:

> one launch path, one identity, one process lineage, one recovery path, one log, one health truth.

No heroics. No ritual. No babysitting.

issues.description:
## Objective

Make Linear the traceable mandate/control layer for Hermes while preserving uc.db/WorkGraph as sovereign execution state.

## Antigravity lane

* Reuse the existing Antigravity conversation **V3 Analysis And Audit**.
* **Do not create a new Antigravity conversation** for PR work.
* `HERMES_ANTIGRAVITY` is the dedicated manager for PR review, conflict resolution, checks and merges through **Orca Computer Use**.
* `HERMES_JULES` remains dedicated to Jules execution/supervision.
* Hermes may read GitHub state with CLI/API for evidence, but must not bypass the Antigravity lane by performing the merge itself.

## First target

PR #37 linked to [KER-9](https://linear.app/aspace-os/issue/KER-9/hc-implement-harness-capability-contract-evidencelevel) / work_id 165, then triage other open Aspace_OS_V3 PRs against current Tech OS Linear/WorkGraph work.

## Traceability protocol

While Desktop Commander is available and Linear is active:

1. A new user mandate is first materialized as a Linear issue in the appropriate Tech OS project.
2. The mandate issue records objective, scope, constraints, target harness/session, acceptance criteria and source issue/work_id.
3. Dispatch to Hermes is recorded in Linear with Hermes lane/session and Orca provenance.
4. Hermes records meaningful action deltas as comments: delegation, harness/session reuse or creation, conflict resolution, test/check result, PR/commit/evidence, blocker/escalation.
5. Technical execution remains bound to uc.db/WorkGraph; Linear is the human-readable backlog and audit projection.
6. Status semantics: Backlog/Todo = not dispatched; In Progress = executing; In Review = acceptance/review pending; Done = durable evidence + acceptance satisfied.
7. Do not create duplicate live sessions for the same work.
8. Do not create new Linear projects for individual problems; issues live inside Tech OS — Kernel Core / Life Core / Buzz Core.

## Acceptance

* Existing Antigravity **V3 Analysis And Audit** session is selected and reused.
* PR #37 mandate is delivered to that existing session through Computer Use.
* No new Antigravity conversation is created.
* Future actions are traceable through Linear comments plus linked uc.db/WorkGraph evidence.
